line: There is a mathematical proof
that if you seal an apple inside a box
and wait for an extremely long time,
that apple can reform.
Let's talk about it.
Imagine a perfectly insulated,
airtight box with an apple inside,
where all the air has been pumped out.
Now, what does the
Second Law of Thermodynamics say will happen?
The apple will slowly decompose,
and its atoms will spread
throughout the entire box.
But look closely:
every single atom of the apple
is still inside that box.
Only their arrangement has changed,
and they are constantly in motion.
Now, how can this apple reform?
Behind this lies a mathematical theorem.
In {1890|eighteen ninety},
Henri {Poincaré|pwan karay}
proved that if a closed system
is confined within a finite space,
it will eventually return
arbitrarily close to its initial state—
and this can happen repeatedly.
However, there is another crazy twist.
Returning doesn't mean what you might think.
No one is actively reassembling the apple;
this occurs purely by chance.
Think of it like this:
imagine a computer randomly guessing a password.
If it continues trying endlessly,
theoretically one day
it will guess the correct password.
The apple's "password"
is more than ten trillion trillion characters long.
That means every single atom of the apple
must be in the exact right place
and moving in the exact right direction.
"Arbitrarily close" means
the apple won't be perfectly identical,
but it will be close enough
that you wouldn't even notice the difference.
So, how long would you have to wait for this?
This {timescale|time scale} grows exponentially
with the number of atoms.
In {2024|twenty twenty four}, Dominik Levesque
and Nicolas {Sourlas|soor lah} simulated a gas
and estimated that even with just a few hundred particles,
such a crude return could take longer
than the age of the universe.
If we're talking about an entire apple,
the number of years required to wait
would contain hundreds of billions of trillions of digits.
Yet, the moment the apple reappears,
its atoms will still be in constant motion,
and it would immediately fall apart again.
So physics says the apple will return,
but the wait for it to reform is so long
that you won't be around to observe it.
